## Citation

Tang, G., Ruiz, T., Barrantes-Reynolds, R., & Mintz, K.P. (2007). Molecular Heterogeneity of EmaA, an Oligomeric Autotransporter Adhesin of *Aggregatibacter Actinomycetemcomitans*. *Microbiology*, 153(Pt 8), 2447-2457.

## Abstract

*Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans* (formerly *Actinobacillus actinomycetemcomitans*) is an oral pathogen associated with aggressive periodontitis. EmaA is an outer membrane autotransporter adhesin involved in bacterial adherence. This study characterizes the molecular structure and heterogeneity of the EmaA protein.

## Key Findings

- EmaA exists as an oligomeric complex on the bacterial surface
- Structural heterogeneity in protein processing and organization
- Variable forms of EmaA contribute to adhesion function
- Implications for bacterial virulence and host-pathogen interactions
- Insights into autotransporter protein biology

## Methods

- Protein purification and characterization
- Electron microscopy and structural analysis
- Biochemical assays of protein-protein interactions
- Bioinformatics analysis of protein structure

## Role

As a co-author, I contributed bioinformatics analysis of protein sequence and structural predictions.
